svg.aria-label: How to write ઘર: 2 letters, ઘ, ર, one after another
svg.title: Writing ઘર
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: ઘ, ર (gujarati). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ઘ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઘ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ર: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ર animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: ઘ: The teaching app animates ઘ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left, circles through the upper lobe, turns back left through the middle, then continues clockwise around the rounded lower body and finishes at its upper right. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the full right spine before turning through its lower foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the upper lobe, middle turn, rounded lower body, and tall right spine, but its printed lobes are broader and the spine foot more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's joined-upper-and-lower-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the lobes, turn, spine, and terminals differently. ર: The teaching app animates ર as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, circles clockwise around the rounded upper body, narrows through the middle, curls around the small middle loop, then descends diagonally into the lower-right tail without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper body, narrow middle, small loop, and descending tail, but its printed turns are wider and more angular and its tail broader than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-body-to-middle-loop-to-lower-tail order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, loop, tail, and terminals differently.
